competencies.justification: Three central sections (Distribution of Water and Land, Oceans, Continents) compel students to explain global ocean and landmass phenomena and their spatial distribution — the chapter would have no purpose without it.

The 'Oceans and Life' section contains a self-contained passage dedicated to ocean conservation — pollution, overfishing, and the collective responsibility to protect oceans — which makes it a major strand.

The correlation between ocean availability and livelihoods (fishing, trade, migration, monsoon-dependent agriculture) is developed genuinely across three named sections ('Oceans', 'Oceans and disasters', 'Oceans and Life'), which makes it a major strand.

The 'Islands' section contains a named sidebar whose primary subject includes India's two major island groups (Andaman & Nicobar, Lakshadweep) and the Indian Antarctica Programme, engaging students with India's topographic diversity.
